applied.fact: Rope note describes a different White Mountain

fitnessSpec.hiking: very high fitness required; approach is a multi-day backpack through the Duckabush / La Crosse-area trail system into the southern interior of the park before any scrambling begins
fitnessSpec.packWeight: multi-day/overnight backpacking load (tent, food, navigation gear) rather than a single-push day pack, given the remote approach

partner_requirements.approachTime: multi-day approach (likely 2+ days each way) via Duckabush / La Crosse Basin / O'Neil Pass trails into the southern interior before the Class 2-3 summit scramble
requiredSkills: off-trail routefinding and navigation (map/compass/GPS) in a remote, sparsely-traveled area
snow travel / ice axe self-arrest for lingering snowfields
wilderness self-sufficiency and self-rescue judgment, since access is committing and self-evacuation distances are long
backcountry camping/permit logistics for a multi-day Olympic National Park trip
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: intermediate-to-advanced scrambler comfortable with off-trail Class 2-3 terrain and committing, self-supported wilderness travel - not a beginner objective given the remote access and long self-evacuation distances already noted

before.rope_note: Could not find a route-specific source for this particular White Mountain (Olympic Mountains, Grand Valley/Hurricane Ridge area); inferred as a non-technical Class 2 talus/ridge scramble.
